aggregation_unit: fresh-process arithmetic mean of its two measured windows
limitations: Two fresh processes per principal role, each with two measured windows; warmups excluded. Tokens and repeated windows within a process are correlated, not independent statistical replications.
The three diagnostic roles have one fresh process each. Run order was not a randomized balanced factorial experiment; no confidence interval or universal throughput superiority is claimed.
The workload is an offline finite actor test, not an HTTP arrival-rate/capacity experiment. Gap counts above 100 ms are descriptive and do not establish HTTP Goodput.

Mixed generated trajectories differ between main, async and native. Whole-window runtime differences are not a pure isolated scheduler-cost measurement; synthetic output matching does not replace task-quality evaluation.
P99 figures are arithmetic averages of per-window P99 values, not a percentile recomputed from pooling runs. Worst-gap ranges cover observed measured windows, not population bounds.
All native reference plugin-specific graph/group counters are null because those workers have no plugin controller. This does not establish that native graph execution is absent.
Readback snapshots and counters were collected outside timing. Group returns and captured-replay calls do not prove hardware resource partitioning or simultaneous kernel execution.
Lifecycle runs are excluded from this performance report and audited separately.
